newsitem.title: UK: Abbey ceo spoke in favour of NatWest merger-report.
newsitem.headline: Abbey ceo spoke in favour of NatWest merger-report.

text.p: Chief executive of Britain's Abbey National Peter Birch spoke two weeks ago in favour of a merger with National Westminster Bank, but opposition was so intense the Abbey National board unanimously rejected the proposal, the Sunday Telegraph newspaper said.

A report in last week's Sunday Telegraph said NatWest had approached Abbey National to discuss merging to create a financial services giant, but Abbey had rejected the idea after "tentatively exploring" it.
Both banks have so far failed to confirm talks took place, but shares in the banks rose on Friday amid renewed reports of a merger, and analysts said the match would be a good fit.
In its latest report the Sunday Telegraph quoted a "Birch admirer" who said, "Dramatic events could still come to pass. This issue is in the hands of the shareholders now."
Meanwhile, the Sunday Times said NatWest was facing pressure from investors to produce a new merger plan after being rebuffed by Abbey National.
Six of NatWest's big institutional investors privately expressed concern at the bank's share price performance, the newspaper said.
A NatWest official declined to comment on the reports. No one at Abbey National could be reached for comment.
